answer: Each challenge is derived from a specified future drand quicknet round, so its threshold-BLS beacon output is publicly verifiable but unpredictable when an agent commits. Binding the commitment to the agent and round prevents a swarm from precomputing answers or replaying cached work across identities; verification also checks the reveal against that exact pulse. The tide, hollow, and ridge labels can domain-separate task families, while admission limits remain necessary because beacon unpredictability alone cannot stop identity creation.
